caption: OOS Sharpe across the floored quarterly lead grid L1–L5. Bars are the best valid combo at each lead; the vermillion line traces the winner's own signal (the HMM wage-stress probability). The published winner (star) sits at L4q with OOS Sharpe 1.41 and is the grid maximum. Unlike the old look-ahead-tainted winner (which was negative at short leads), this signal's curve is POSITIVE at every scanned lead and peaks at L4q — internally consistent. But the grid is short (only L1–L5), every point is search-conditioned on a 25-quarter window, and the causality tests say the indicator is lagging — treat the ridge as descriptive, not a forecasting edge.
narrative_alignment_note: Published L4q winner is the grid maximum and its own lead-curve peaks there; honest note that the grid is short and search-conditioned.
